note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Are relief and vent flows to the flare or atmosphere unmetered?

evidence.text: stream V-B (asset stream:V-B) reads "VENT HEADER TO FLARE"
no flow measurement on these streams

data_requests.item: Flare or vent flow and composition
where: a walkdown: ultrasonic flare-gas meter or a temporary vent flow measurement
site records: relief valve lift records
data_requests.how: Separate continuous (background) flow from relief events.

questions.decision_rule: Worth metering when background flow is continuous; relief-only lines that seldom lift close the question.

typical_benefit.wording: Background flaring "can be as much as 50% of all flared gases (Miles, 2001)." In refineries it "will generally be less than 50%." No recovery % stated.
source_titles: S19: Worrell & Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Petroleum Refineries: An ENERGY STAR Guide (LBNL-56183, Feb 2005)

questions.limits: Relief paths are safety systems; metering or recovery changes go through a hazard review.
